```{python}
    columns=["model", "mpg", "cyl", "disp", "hp", "drat", "wt"],

def typst_table(df: pd.DataFrame, width: str = "80%", notes: str | None = None) -> Markdown:
    """Render a pandas DataFrame as a booktabs-style Typst table with optional notes."""
    ncols = len(df.columns)
    cols_spec = "(" + ", ".join(["1fr"] * ncols) + ")"
    align_spec = "(" + ", ".join(["right"] * ncols) + ")"
    header_cells = ", ".join(f"[{col}]" for col in df.columns)

    body_lines = []
    for _, row in df.iterrows():
        cells = ", ".join(f"[{val}]" for val in row)
        body_lines.append(f"      {cells},")

    note_block = ""
    if notes:
        note_block = f"\n  #align(left)[#text(size: 0.85em)[{notes}]]"

    fence = "`" * 3
    typst_code = "\n".join(
        [
            f"{fence}{{=typst}}",
            f"#block(width: {width})[",
            "  #table(",
            f"    columns: {cols_spec},",
            f"    align: {align_spec},",
            "    stroke: none,",
            "    table.hline(stroke: 0.08em),",
            f"    table.header({header_cells}),",
            "    table.hline(stroke: 0.05em),",
            *body_lines,
            "    table.hline(stroke: 0.08em),",
            f"  ){note_block}",
            "]",
            fence,
        ]
    )
    return Markdown(typst_code)
```

This document shows a minimal Python example of the template.
For more information, see the full Python example in `template-full-python.qmd`.

# Section as Heading Level 1

Section numbering can be specified in the YAML `section-numbering` field
as other Typst templates.

## Subsection as Heading Level 2

You can use LaTeX math expressions:

$$
Y_{it} = \alpha_i + \lambda_t + \sum_{k \neq -1} \tau_h \mathbb{1}\{E_i + k = t\} +
\varepsilon_{it}.
$$

### Subsubsection as Heading Level 3

I don't use and don't recommend using heading levels 3 and below but it works.

## Citation

You can cite a reference like this [@katsushika1831] or @horst2020.
Typst has some built-in citation styles. Check the [Typst documentation](https://typst.app/docs/reference/model/bibliography/#parameters-style) for more information.

# Figures and Tables

## Figures

As @fig-hist-mpg shows, the caption is displayed below the figure.
As a caption of the figure (`fig-cap`), I use bold text for the title and use a normal text for the description.

```{python}
#| label: fig-hist-mpg
#| fig-cap: "**Histogram of Miles per Gallon**. The x-axis shows the miles per gallon, and the y-axis shows the frequency."

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
ax.hist(mtcars["mpg"], bins=5, color="lightgray", edgecolor="black")
ax.set_title("Histogram of mtcars.mpg")
ax.set_xlabel("mpg")
ax.set_ylabel("Frequency")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Tables

You can render booktabs-style academic tables directly to Typst from `pandas` using a lightweight helper function (or packages such as `great_tables` / `tabulate`).^[Generating raw Typst `#table(...)` blocks gives full control over booktabs rules, column spans, and table notes with no R dependency.]
As @tbl-mtcars-head shows, the caption is displayed above the table.
The notes of the table can be added using the `notes` argument of the `typst_table()` helper function.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-mtcars-head
#| tbl-cap: Head of the mtcars Dataset

nt = "_Notes_: This table shows the first five rows of the mtcars dataset."
typst_table(mtcars.iloc[:5, :5], width="80%", notes=nt)
```

# Last words

I made this template for my working papers, so it may not be suitable for other fields than economics.
I am happy to receive feedback and suggestions for improvement.

{{< appendix >}}

# Supplemental Figures

The figure numbering will be reset to "A.1", "A.2", etc so that it is clear that these figures are part of the appendix.

```{python}
#| label: fig-scatter-car
#| fig-cap: "**Scatter Plot of Car Data**. The x-axis shows the weight of the car, and the y-axis shows the miles per gallon."

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
ax.scatter(mtcars["wt"], mtcars["mpg"], facecolors="none", edgecolors="black")
ax.set_xlabel("wt")
ax.set_ylabel("mpg")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
